subject.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full

question: Should `security=full` bypass the ambiguous-interpreter script-preflight rejection for approval-gated `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always` modes, or only for YOLO `ask=off`?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow, but code review cannot decide whether approval-gated full-security commands should lose this fail-closed defense-in-depth check.

options.title: Accept full-security bypass with docs alignment
options.body: Treat `security=full` as the trust boundary regardless of ask mode, update `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md` to match, and re-review after the doc fix.

options.title: Keep bypass YOLO-only
options.body: Preserve the existing `security=full` plus `ask=off` contract and revise code/docs so approval-gated modes still use the ambiguous-interpreter heuristic.

options.title: Pause pending security direction
options.body: Hold or close this PR until the linked protected issue gets an explicit maintainer security-policy decision.

recommendation.title: Accept full-security bypass with docs alignment
recommendation.body: Treat `security=full` as the trust boundary regardless of ask mode, update `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md` to match, and re-review after the doc fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest history on host-exec YOLO policy and the approval docs that define the current boundary.
